title: Zhiyi
hookLine: the founder of Tiantai, who ordered all the sutras into one great system

lines: A MONK SETS OUT TO SORT IT.
cards: A lot of kitchens have that one drawer. Batteries, twist ties, a key to nothing, a birthday candle. Everything in it is useful, and nothing can be found.
Chinese Buddhists once had a drawer like that, only it was full of sutras. Teachings arrived from India and Central Asia over a long time, translated by different people, in no particular order.
Some seemed simple, some soaring, and some seemed to say opposite things. Which one came first? Which one was the heart?
A monk on a mountain set out to sort the whole drawer. Today, Zhiyi.

teach.b: First, the man and the mountain. Zhiyi is honored as the founder of the Tiantai school, which takes its name from Mount Tiantai, where he lived and taught. Second, the sorting.
Zhiyi's answer to the contradictions was not to throw any sutra out.

He arranged them as stages of the Buddha's teaching life, and as different kinds of teaching for different listeners. A doctor gives one patient a mild medicine and another a strong one, and both are right.
In his scheme, the simpler sutras prepare the way, and the Lotus Sutra stands at the summit, where all the paths turn out to be one. Third, the practice behind the system.

His lectures on meditation, written down by a student, are called Mohe Zhiguan, the great calming and contemplation. Calming settles the mind, like still water. Contemplation looks clearly at what's there.
He taught them as two wings of one bird, and he wrote practical advice on posture, food, sleep and breath. Fourth, what a system is for.
For Zhiyi, putting every teaching in its place was a kind of respect: nothing wasted, nothing rejected, every sutra with a job.
Other Chinese schools sorted the sutras differently, and Tiantai's order was not the only one. But his drawer, once sorted, could be opened by anyone.

how: In Tiantai (Tendai in Japan, Cheontae in Korea) communities, practitioners study the Lotus Sutra and Zhiyi's writings and practice calming and contemplation meditation as he described it.

games.q: two sutras seem to say opposite things. you're Zhiyi. what do you do?
o: decide one is fake and drop it
place each where it fits in the Buddha's teaching
games.why: Zhiyi treated them like medicines for different patients: both right, each in its place, all leading to the Lotus Sutra.

practice: Let the breath calm down; that's the calming. Then, as each thought arrives, give it a quiet label, planning, remembering, worrying, hearing, set it on its shelf, and come back to the breath.
Nothing gets thrown out; that's the contemplation, seeing clearly what's there.

wordCard.voice: Zhiyi. The founder of the Tiantai school, who ordered the sutras into one system with the Lotus Sutra at the summit, and taught calming and contemplation. Today's word.

orig.note: Chinese zhiguan: calming and contemplation, the heart of Zhiyi's meditation teaching.

carryVoice: Your line: everything in its place. Nothing wasted, and every sutra with a job. That's day nine hundred eighty-four.
